I found the root cause: this `TodayScreen.swift` file already had a partial fix attempted (hoisting `dateKey`/`recipe`/`shareableImage` into `let` bindings before the `ShareLink` call), but it still failed to compile because the `ShareLink(item: shareableImage) { ... }` call was still living inside a `@ViewBuilder` closure (the `HStack` in `revealedState`). Swift's ViewBuilder type-checker was still trying to solve the `ShareLink`/`Transferable` generic overload jointly with the rest of the `HStack`'s children, and choking with "no exact matches in call to initializer" even though `ShareableAuraImage` genuinely conforms to `Transferable` correctly (verified `Services/Export/ExportPipeline.swift`'s conformance is sound).

**Fix**: extracted the share button into its own plain (non-`@ViewBuilder`) function `shareButton(mood:chips:)` in `UI/Screens/TodayScreen.swift`, so the `ShareLink` initializer is type-checked in isolation via an explicit `return` statement, decoupled from the surrounding `HStack`'s builder inference. The `HStack` in `revealedState` now just calls `shareButton(mood: mood, chips: chips)` plus the existing `Regenerate` button — no behavior change, same accessibility identifiers/labels.

Note: I wasn't able to re-run `xcodebuild`/`xcrun`/`swift` in this sandbox to verify directly — every invocation was blocked with "This command requires approval" and never granted, so I couldn't get a fresh compiler confirmation. I did exhaustively verify by static analysis that every type in the chain (`ShareableAuraImage`, `AuraRecipe`, `MoodID`, `EntitlementSnapshot`, etc.) is correctly `Sendable`/`Transferable`, and this extraction pattern is the standard fix for spurious "no exact matches" errors caused by ViewBuilder inference complexity.
